stem.en: Kabir tunes the feedback so strong that a single product molecule shuts the first enzyme completely. What happens to the factory?

text.en: It flickers. One molecule shuts it; the molecule is used; it opens; makes one; shuts. The level is always near zero and the cell is always just short. Feedback is meant to lean, not slam.
It runs perfectly with no waste.

feedback.en: Tight control that overshoots to zero is a shortage. The cell needs a steady supply, which needs a gradual lean.
Strong feedback slows the first enzyme harder. It is a brake, and this is the brake jammed on.
Nothing is ignored. The enzyme shuts, exactly as set.

explanation.en: Good feedback is proportional. A little product, a little slowing; a lot, a lot. Le Chatelier's lean, from III.6, built into a fold.
